The dog-bone samples were sealed in an evacuated quartz tube maintained about 0.67 Pa vacuum and annealed at 1200 °C for 45 min and quenched in water to achieve recrystallized microstructures.
The XRD patterns in Fig. 3 a show a single set of BCC diffraction peaks, confirming that the as-cast alloys are BCC single-phase solid solutions, consistent with empirical and CALPHAD predictions.

Fig. 5 illustrates the EBSD inverse pole figures (IPF) and BCC phase maps of the annealed samples, which now display a random, equiaxed grain structure indicative of a single-phase BCC solid solution.
Fig. 4 presents the backscattered images and elemental EDS mappings of as-cast HfxNbTaTiV alloys, revealing uniform dendritic microstructures devoid of secondary phase precipitates.

Fig. 5 illustrates the EBSD inverse pole figures (IPF) and BCC phase maps of the annealed samples, which now display a random, equiaxed grain structure indicative of a single-phase BCC solid solution.
The secondary dendrite arm spacing increases with Hf content, suggesting that Hf enhances undercooling at the dendrite tips during solidification [52,53].

Pronounced microsegregation is evident in the EDS mappings, with elements like Ta and Nb, which have higher melting points, concentrating in dendritic cores, and elements such as Hf, Ti, and V, with lower melting points, segregating in interdendritic regions.

evidence.section: 3.5 Solid solution strengthening and lattice distortion
evidence.quote: The increase of lattice distortion induced by Hf addition plays a key role in strengthening RMPEAs.
Theoretical analyses indicate that solid solution strengthening is the primary mechanism responsible for strengthening these alloys.

A series of HfxNbTaTiV (x = 0.00, 0.25, 0.50, 0.75, 1.00 in molar ratio) alloy ingots with different Hf content were synthesized from high purity (>99.95%) metals by vacuum arc melting within a Ti-gettered ultra-high purity Ar (>99.99%) atmosphere.
The button-shaped ingots were rolled into thin sheets approximately 1 mm in thick at room temperature using a precision rolling mill (JH-RZH-110, China).
